blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning for instruction-guided image editing requires reward models that provide reliable, accurate, and efficient feedback. Direct scalar prediction compresses multidimensional editing preferences, whereas generative evaluators can expose their judgment through explicit reasoning. However, broad scoring criteria do not specify all instance-dependent editing and preservation constraints, and generating long reasoning trajectories is costly for online optimization. We introduce CheckDistill, a pointwise reward modeling framework that internalizes instruction-adaptive checklists. We decompose each editing condition into atomic, independently verifiable requirements and construct four-dimensional scoring labels together with structured verification evidence. After supervised score initialization, a privileged teacher conditions on checklists, item-level judgments, and dimension-level rationales to supervise the student's own scoring trajectories. A reliability-weighted on-policy self-distillation objective adjusts supervision at score tokens according to agreement between the teacher's expected scores and reference labels, while retaining candidate probability weights in a truncated token support. The deployed student directly predicts four score distributions without checklist inputs or explicit reasoning and aggregates their expectations into a scalar reward. CheckDistill achieves aggregate accuracies of 72.30%, 56.67% and 82.90% on MMRB2, MER-Bench and EditReward-Bench, respectively, exceeding the compared open-source baselines on all three metrics.
blocks.zh: 加强教学指导图像编辑的学习需要提供可靠、准确和高效反馈的奖励模式。 直接的scalar预测压缩了多维编辑偏好,而基因评价者可以通过明确的推理来暴露他们的判断. 然而,广泛的评分标准并未具体指明所有依实例进行的编辑和保存限制,而产生长推理轨迹对于网上优化来说成本高昂. 我们引入了CheckDistill,一个有分寸的奖赏模型框架,将指令调整清单内部化. 我们把每个编辑条件分解成原子,独立可核查的要求,并结合结构化的核查证据构建出四维分数标签. 监督分数初始化后,教师在核对表,项目级判断和维度级原理上享有特权条件,以监督学生自己的分数轨迹. 可靠性加权的政策自消化目标根据教师预期分数与参考分数之间的协议,调整分数符上的监督,同时将候选人概率分数保留在短符号支持中. 被部署的学生直接预测4个分数分布,没有核对表输入或明确推理,并将其期望汇总为分数奖励. 在MMRB2、MER-Bench和Edit-Reward-Bench上,CheckDistill分别实现72.30%、56.67%和82.90%的总加速率,超过了所有三个指标的开源基线。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Instruction-guided image editing is a key application of multi-modal generation, enabling users to perform diverse image modifications through natural language instructions. Reinforcement learning can substantially improve image editing performance, with reward models playing a critical role in guiding optimization. An effective reward model must evaluate candidate results across complementary dimensions, distinguish subtle yet consequential differences, and provide accurate preference rankings and score singals. Frequent reward queries during online reinforcement learning further require reward models to combine comprehensive, fine-grained evaluation with efficient scoring.
blocks.zh: 指令制导的图像编辑是多模式生成的关键应用,使用户能够通过自然语言指令进行多样的图像修改. 强化学习可以大幅度地提高图像编辑性能,奖励模式在引导优化中发挥关键作用. 有效的奖励模式必须评估候选人在互补层面的结果,区分微妙而间接的差异,并提供准确的优惠排名和得分单曲。 在线强化学习期间频繁的奖励查询进一步要求奖励模式将综合,精细的评价与高效的分数相结合.

blocks.en: Existing reward modeling approaches do not fully meet these requirements. As shown in Fig. 1 (a), regression-based reward models ( Xu et al., 2023 ; Wu et al., 2023a ; Wu et al., 2026 ) enable efficient scoring. However, these models rely on coarse-grained subjective preferences, typically learned through pairwise objectives such as the Bradley–Terry loss ( Bradley and Terry, 1952 ) . These objectives alone provide neither explicit verification evidence nor absolute score calibration. These limitations reduce interpretability and may make score distributions more prone to drift and the models more vulnerable to reward hacking. Fig. 1 (b) shows the reasoning-based generative reward models ( Luo et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026a ; Kan et al., 2026 ) . This paradigm uses fixed rubric prompts to guide evaluation through explicit reasoning before scoring. However, even when rubrics are generated adaptively, dimension-level prompts may leave concrete verification targets insufficiently specified. The resulting reasoning may not systematically cover the instance-specific editing and preservation constraints that distinguish otherwise similar candidates. Moreover, reasoning-based scoring requires additional autoregressive decoding at each evaluation. Although downstream optimization uses the resulting reward scores, generating the accompanying rationales adds latency and limits throughput during online RL training.
blocks.zh: 现有的奖励模式办法不能完全满足这些要求。 如图1(a)所示,基于回归的奖励模式(徐等,2023;吴等,2023a; Wu et al., 2026 ))可以实现高效得分. 然而,这些模型依赖于粗糙的主观偏好,通常通过双向目标学习,如布拉德利-特瑞损失(Bradley and Terry, 1952). 这些目标本身既不提供明确的核查证据,也不提供绝对分数校正。 这些限制降低了可解释性,并可能使分数分配更容易被漂移,而模型更容易被奖励黑客. 图1(b)显示了基于推理的基因奖励模型(Luo等,2026;Wang等,2026a; Kan等, 2026 (英语). 这个范式在打分前使用固定的标点提示来通过明确的推理来指导评价. 然而,即使随机生成数字,尺寸级提示可能使具体的核查目标不够明确。 由此得出的推理可能没有系统地涵盖区分其他类似候选人的具体案例编辑和保存限制。 此外,基于推理的评分要求在每个评价中增加自动解码。 虽然下游优化使用由此得到的奖励分数,但是在在线RL培训中,生成配套的理由增加了耐久性和限制吞吐量.

blocks.en: These limitations motivate two complementary principles. First, Dynamic Checklist Scaling : reward judgments should be grounded in instance-adaptive identification of editing and preservation requirements, decomposed into fine-grained, atomic, and independently verifiable checks. Expanding the coverage and specificity of these checks can support more accurate and robust reward judgments. Second, Context-Compressed Reward Scoring : efficient online deployment requires reducing the decoding overhead of lengthy chain-of-thought reasoning context while preserving reward quality. Therefore, the core challenge is to align score distributions under standard editing inputs with their evidence-conditioned counterparts, while reducing inference-time dependence on extensive verification contexts and explicit reasoning.
blocks.zh: 这些限制激励了两项相辅相成的原则。 首先,动态核对清单缩放:奖励判决应基于对编辑和保存要求的根据具体情况确定,分解为精细、原子和可独立核查的检查。 扩大这些检查的覆盖面和特殊性可以支持更准确和有力的奖励判决。 第二,上下文压缩奖励标准:有效的在线部署需要减少长时间思维推理链的解码间接费用,同时保持奖励质量。 因此,核心挑战是如何使标准编辑投入下的分数分配与其有证据条件的对应方保持一致,同时减少推断时间对广泛核查背景和明确推理的依赖。

blocks.en: Guided by these principles, we propose CheckDistill , an image editing reward modeling framework that combines dynamic checklist-based data construction with reliability-aware on-policy self-distillation, as illustrated in Fig. 1 (c). The framework builds structured verification evidence during training and transfers evidence-enhanced judgments into efficient direct scoring.
blocks.zh: 在这些原则的指导下,我们提议建立一个图像编辑奖励模型框架,将基于清单的动态数据构建与可靠意识的政策自我消化结合起来,如图1(c)所示。 该框架在培训过程中建立结构化的核查证据,并将加强证据判断转化为有效的直接评分。

blocks.en: For data construction, Fig. 2 illustrates how the source image and editing instruction guide atomic checks for Instruction Following (IF), Attribute Preservation (AP), and Context Preservation (CP). These checks are shared across candidates under the same editing condition. In the illustrated example, item-level judgments identify an unchanged like count and an undeleted comment, while separately verifying preservation requirements. Perceptual Quality (PQ) is assessed independently using a fixed general rubric. Combining EditReward-Data ( Wu et al., 2026 ) with additional Qwen-Image-Edit ( Wu et al., 2025a ) candidates, we construct CheckDistill-40K through this annotation pipeline and human preference-consistency filtering, pairing four-dimensional score labels with item-level judgments and dimension-level rationales.
blocks.zh: 在数据构建方面,图2说明了源图像和编辑指导如何指导“指令跟随”(IF)、属性保存(AP)和背景保存(CP)的原子检查。 这些检查由候选人在同样的编辑条件下分享。 在示例中,项级判决确定一个与计数和未删除的评论一样不变,同时单独核实保存要求。 认知质量(PQ)使用固定的一般标点进行独立评估. 将"Edit Reward-Data"(Wu等,2026年)与额外的"Quen-Image-Edit"(Wu等,2025a年)入选者合并,我们通过这个注释管道和人类偏好相容性过滤,将四维分数标签与项目级判断和维度级原理相配.

blocks.en:
CheckDistill adopts two-stage training. Mixed SFT first establishes direct scoring and checklist-guided reasoning capabilities. Then we introduce Checklist-Guided Reliability-Aware On-Policy Self-Distillation (CR-OPSD) .
The teacher additionally receives checklists, item-level judgments, and dimension-level rationales, providing distributional supervision on response prefixes generated by a student that observes only standard editing inputs. Since evidence-enhanced predictions may still be unreliable, we use agreement between the teacher’s expected score and the reference label as a reliability proxy to modulate distillation at the four score positions. At inference time, only the student is retained, and expected scores from its four-dimensional score distributions are aggregated into a scalar reward, without additional verification context or lengthy rationale generation.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are as follows: • Dynamic checklist-based reward supervision. We construct CheckDistill-40K , pairing four-dimensional scores with instance-specific verification evidence through dynamic checklists and human preference-consistency filtering. • Reliability-aware distillation for efficient reward scoring. We propose CR-OPSD to transfer evidence-conditioned scoring behavior into a direct reward model through reliability-aware on-policy distribution alignment. • Leading reward accuracy and downstream editing gains. blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning (RL) ( Black et al., 2024 ; Fan et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2025a ; Xue et al., 2025 ; Zheng et al., 2026 ) has emerged as an important post-training paradigm for visual generation, enabling diffusion and flow-based models ( Rombach et al., 2022 ; Podell et al., 2024 ; Esser et al., 2024 ; Black Forest Labs et al., 2025 ) to achieve stronger alignment. Its effectiveness, however, relies heavily on accurate and efficient reward models.
blocks.zh: 强化学习(RL)(Black等,2024;Fan等,2023;Liu等,2025a;Xue等,2025;Zheng等,2026)已作为视觉生成,能传播和以流为主的模型(Rombach等,2022;Podel等,2024;Esser等,2024;Black Forest Labs等,2025)的重要培训后范例而出现,以达到更强的校正. 然而,其效力在很大程度上取决于准确而有效的奖励模式。

blocks.en: Regression-based visual reward models learn human preferences from vision-language representations using regression or Bradley–Terry-style preference objectives ( Wu et al., 2023b ; Xu et al., 2023 ; Kirstain et al., 2023 ; Wu et al., 2023a ; Zhang et al., 2024b ; Wu et al., 2024b ; Zhang et al., 2024a ; Chen et al., 2025 ; Ma et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025b ; Wu et al., 2026 ) . These methods are efficient at inference, but typically output scalar scores without explicit reasoning, limiting interpretability and diagnostic feedback for fine-grained evaluation.
blocks.zh: 基于后退的视觉奖励模型利用回归或Bradley-Terry风格的偏好目标从视觉语言表述中学习人类偏好(Wu等,2023b;Xu等,2023;Kirstain等,2023;Wu等,2023a; 张等,2024b;吴等,2024b;张等,2024a;陈等,2025;马等,2025;王等,2025b;吴等,2026. 这些方法在推论上是高效的,但典型的输出分数却没有明确的推理,限制了可解释性和对精细评价的诊断反馈.

blocks.en: Generative reward models such as EditScore ( Luo et al., 2026 ) , RationalRewards ( Wang et al., 2026a ) , SpatialReward ( Long et al., 2026 ) , and UnifiedReward-Think ( Wang et al., 2025a ) produce explicit rationales or chain-of-thought reasoning for fine-grained reward prediction under fixed evaluation criteria. However, these criteria are not instantiated into concrete, input-specific verification requirements, and inference-time reasoning introduces substantial overhead in large-scale online RL. JRM ( Yang et al., 2026 ) and Z-Reward ( Jin et al., 2026 ) improve efficiency by internalizing reasoning into direct reward prediction, but still lack instance-adaptive verification criteria.
blocks.zh: EditScore(Luo等,2026年),"理性奖励"等基因奖励模型 (Wang等,2026a).,"空间奖励". (Long等,2026年),"统一奖励-思考"(Wang等,2025a)为固定评价标准下的精细奖励预测提出了明确的理由或思路链. 然而,这些标准并没有被立即纳入具体的、针对具体投入的核查要求,推论时间推理在大规模在线RL中引入了大量的间接费用。 JRM (Yang等,2026年)和Z-Reward (Jin等,2026年)通过将推理内部化为直接奖励预测来提高效率,但仍缺乏实例适应性验证标准.

blocks.en: Instance-adaptive methods tailor evaluation criteria to each input. RubricRM ( Kan et al., 2026 ) generates input-specific dimensions and scoring criteria, but remains focused on high-level evaluation dimensions. Edit-R1 ( Guo et al., 2026 ) decomposes editing instructions into sample-specific principles for finer-grained verification, but still requires explicit reasoning at inference time. Checklist-based methods translate evaluation requirements into directly verifiable items ( Cook et al., 2024 ) ; rDPO ( Yu et al., 2026 ) , for example, constructs instance-specific checklist-style rubrics primarily for preference data construction. In contrast, CheckDistill uses source-image-grounded atomic checklists only as privileged information during reward-model training, distilling fine-grained instance-specific verification requirements into direct reward prediction without checklist generation or explicit reasoning at inference time.
blocks.zh: 实例适应方法使评价标准与每项投入相适应。 RubricRM(Kan等,2026年)生成出针对输入的维度和评分标准,但仍以高评价维度为主. Edit-R1 (Guo等,2026年)将编辑指令分解为取自样本的特定原理来进行更细的刻度验证,但仍需在推论时明确推理. 基于核对清单的方法将评价要求转化为可直接核查的项目(Cook等,2024年;rDPO(Yu等,2026年)),例如,主要为偏好数据构建构建构建构建实例特定核对清单风格的路由. 相比之下,CheckDistill在奖励模式培训期间仅将来源图像基原子清单用作特权信息,将精细实例特定核查要求提炼成直接奖励预测,而不生成清单,也不在推断时明确推理。

blocks.en: 3.1 Evaluation Formulation
blocks.zh: 3.1 评价

We evaluate image editing from two complementary aspects: Semantic Consistency (SC) and Perceptual Quality (PQ). SC comprises three dimensions: Instruction Following (IF), which measures whether the requested edits are correctly executed; Attribute Preservation (AP), which measures whether unspecified attributes of edited objects are preserved; and Context Preservation (CP), which measures whether non-edited content remains unchanged.
PQ measures the overall visual quality of the edited image.
All four scores, S IF S_{\mathrm{IF}} , S AP S_{\mathrm{AP}} , S CP S_{\mathrm{CP}} , and S PQ S_{\mathrm{PQ}} , are defined on a discrete scale from 0 0 to 9 9 .

blocks.en: 3.2 Reward Data Construction Pipeline

blocks.en: To construct the reward training data, we develop an annotation pipeline that leverages instance-specific checklists to facilitate fine-grained evaluation and reliable score annotation, while also providing structured privileged information for subsequent knowledge internalization via CR-OPSD.

blocks.en: We evaluate input and output scaling on MMRB2 using Qwen3.5-9B, measuring accuracy and output token counts. In Figure 5 , SFT denotes supervised fine-tuning on CheckDistill-40K, while zero-shot refers to evaluation without task-specific fine-tuning.

blocks.en:
Instance-specific verification evidence improves reward judgement through input and output scaling. Supplying a checklist improves zero-shot direct-scoring accuracy from 55.76% to 58.90%, while adding checklist-guided judgements raises it to 70.60%, with about 10 output tokens.
Generating evaluation content also helps: a generic rationale achieves 61.07%, generating a checklist and its guided judgement reaches 62.40%, and supplying the checklist before generating the judgement achieves 63.41%.
These gains support grounding reward assessment in instance-specific verification requirements.
In particular, the strong input-scaling result demonstrates the value of evidence-enriched teacher contexts , motivating Dynamic Checklist Scaling in CheckDistill.
blocks.zh:
具体案例的核查证据通过投入和产出规模改进奖励判断。 提供一份核对表可以提高0发直射精度,从55.76%提高到58.90%,而增加核对表指导判断则将其提高到了70.60%,并有约10个输出符.
生成评价内容也有所帮助:通用理由达到61.07%,生成清单及其指导性判断达到62.40%,在生成判断之前提供清单达到63.41%。
这些收益支持根据具体核查要求确定奖励评估的基础。
特别是,强劲的输入扩展结果表明,在 " CheckDistill " 中,丰富证据的教师环境很有价值,激发了动态核对清单的放大作用。

blocks.en:
CheckDistill retains the benefits of evidence-supported evaluation in a compact, direct-scoring model. SFT achieves 63.50% accuracy with direct scoring and 67.70% when generating a checklist and judgement.
CheckDistill reaches 72.30% with about 10 output tokens, exceeding these configurations by 8.80 and 4.60 percentage points and surpassing the 70.60% zero-shot result with supplied verification evidence.
This supports Distribution-Aligned Context Compression: transferring evidence-enhanced scoring to a student requiring neither verification contexts nor lengthy reasoning at inference time.
Compared with the approximately 700-token SFT reasoning configuration, CheckDistill achieves higher accuracy with approximately 1/70 of the output tokens , demonstrating a favorable accuracy–decoding-cost trade-off.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We present CheckDistill, an efficient reward modeling framework for instruction-guided image editing. It combines instance-specific dynamic checklists for fine-grained verification with CR-OPSD to distill evidence-supported scoring behavior into a direct-scoring model that requires neither checklist inputs nor explicit reasoning at inference time. Experiments demonstrate strong reward modeling performance and improved image editing through reward-guided reinforcement learning using DiffusionNFT. Together, these findings show that scaling instance-specific verification improves reward quality, while reliability-aware distillation enables efficient reward scoring for image editing at scale.
blocks.zh: 我们向您介绍 CheckDistill, 一个用于指导图像编辑的高效奖励模型框架。 它将针对具体实例的动态核对表与CR-OPSD结合,将证据支持的评分行为提炼成直接评分模型,在推断时不需要核对表投入或明确推理. 实验通过使用 DifmusionNFT 的奖励指导强化学习,展现出强有力的奖励模型性能并改进了图像编辑. 这些调查结果加在一起表明,针对具体实例的缩放核查可提高奖励质量,而了解可靠性的蒸馏则能对图像的大规模编辑进行有效奖励。

blocks.en: A.4 Reward Benchmark Evaluation Details
blocks.zh: A.4 奖励基准评价细节

blocks.en:
We evaluate reward prediction on MMRB2, MER-Bench, and EditReward-Bench, none of which overlaps with the data used for CheckDistill.
MMRB2 reports single-reference, multi-reference, and overall accuracy, where the overall accuracy is computed as a sample-count-weighted average of the single- and multi-reference subsets rather than their arithmetic mean. MER-Bench reports ranking accuracy under the 2-pair, 3-pair, and 4-pair settings, with their arithmetic mean used as the overall metric. EditReward-Bench evaluates prompt following (PF), consistency (CS), and overall preference accuracy. For CheckDistill  PF is given by the instruction-following score, while CS is computed from the attribute-preservation (AP) and context-preservation (CP) scores using weights of 0.35 and 0.25, respectively, consistent with their weights in the overall reward. The final scalar reward follows Eq. 8 and 1 . Except for specialized reward models with their own inference formats, all evaluated models use the same system prompt. Each candidate is scored independently in a pointwise manner, after which pairwise comparisons and multi-candidate rankings are obtained by comparing the resulting scalar scores.

我们评价MMRB2、MER-Bench和Edit Reward-Bench的奖励预测,这些预测都与CheckDistill的数据没有重叠。
MMRB2报告单一参考、多参考和总体准确性,其中总体准确性作为单一和多参考子集的抽样加权平均值而不是其算术平均值来计算。 MER-Bench报告在2-pair,3-pair,和4-pair设置下对精确度进行排名,其算术平均值作为总体度量. Edit Reward-Bench 评估了后面的(PF),一致性(CS),以及总体偏好准确性. 检查悬浮 PF由指令后分数给出,而CS则根据属性-保护(AP)和上下文-保护(CP)的分数分别使用0.35和0.25的权重来计算,与它们在总体奖励中的权重一致. 最后的斯卡尔奖跟随Eq. 8和1. 除了具有自己推论格式的专业奖励模型,所有被评价的模型都使用相同的系统即时. 每位考生均以分取出的方式独立得分,之后通过比较产生的分取分取出分取出对等比较和多候选人排名.

blocks.zh: 附录D

blocks.en: Instruction-guided image editing requires models to execute requested transformations while preserving unrelated visual content. Recent open-source and open-weight models, exemplified by Qwen-Image and FLUX.1 Kontext, have substantially expanded the capabilities of language-driven image editing [ Wu et al., 2025a , Black Forest Labs et al., 2025 , Hu et al., 2026a , Meituan LongCat Team et al., 2025 , Wu et al., 2025b , Liu et al., 2025b , Super Intelligence Team, 2026 ]. Capability-centric data design further supports the joint development of generation and editing through coordinated supervision and training curricula [ Wang et al., 2026b ]. Meanwhile, commercial systems such as GPT Image and Gemini bring image generation and editing into interactive creative workflows [ OpenAI, , Google DeepMind, ], while virtual try-on research extends these capabilities toward fashion applications that require faithful preservation of garment appearance and person identity [ Chen et al., 2026 , Choi et al., 2024 , Chong et al., 2024 ]. To assess these increasingly diverse capabilities, benchmarks including GEdit-Bench, ImgEdit-Bench, REDEdit-Bench, and CPI-Bench collectively broaden evaluation across editing tasks and practical usage scenarios [ Liu et al., 2025b , Ye et al., 2025 , Super Intelligence Team, 2026 , Zhou et al., 2026 ]. These developments motivate alignment methods that jointly account for instruction fulfillment, content preservation, and perceptual quality.
blocks.zh: 指令引导的图像编辑需要模型执行所请求的转换,同时保留不相关的视觉内容. 以Quen-Image和FLUX.1 Kontext为例的近期开放源码和开放量模型大大扩展了由语言驱动图像编辑的能力[Wu等,2025a;Black Forest Labs等,2025;Hu等,2026a;Meituan LongCat] Team等,2025年;Wu等,2025年b;Liu等,2025年b;Super Intelligence Team,2026]). 以能力为中心的数据设计进一步支持通过协调的监督和培训课程共同开发生成和编辑[Wang等,2026b]. 同时,GPT Image和双子座等商业系统将图像生成和编辑带入互动的创意工作流程[OpenAI,.,Google DeepMind,],而虚拟尝试研究将这些能力扩展到需要忠实地保存服装外观和人物身份的时尚应用[. Chen等,2026年;Choi等,2024年;Chong等,2024年). 为了评估这些日益多样化的能力,包括Gedit-Bench、ImgEdit-Bench、ReDedit-Bench和CPI-Bench在内的基准共同扩大了对编辑任务和实际使用设想的评价范围[刘等,2025b;叶等,2025;超级情报组,2026;周等,2026]。 这些事态发展促使采用统一方法,共同说明教学的完成、内容保存和观念的质量。

blocks.en: RL provides a post-training mechanism for optimizing visual generators against feedback beyond supervised reconstruction objectives. DDPO and DPOK establish policy-gradient approaches for diffusion models [ Black et al., 2024 , Fan et al., 2023 ] ; Flow-GRPO and DanceGRPO extend group-relative optimization to flow-based and broader visual generation settings [ Liu et al., 2025a , Xue et al., 2025 ] , while DiffusionNFT formulates online reward-driven updates through the forward process [ Zheng et al., 2026 ] . Building on these foundations, editing-specific methods increasingly emphasize the design of reward feedback. HIVE learns human preferences to guide instructional editing [ Zhang et al., 2024a ] . UniWorld-V2 combines DiffusionNFT with MLLM logit-based feedback and group filtering to stabilize editing optimization [ Li et al., 2025 ] . Edit-R1 trains a principle-based reasoning verifier and uses its rewards to optimize editing models with GRPO [ Guo et al., 2026 ] . At the system level, Swift-Image combines parallel expert RL with multi-teacher on-policy distillation to mitigate interference among heterogeneous objectives [ Hu et al., 2026a ] . Together, these approaches motivate rewards that reliably distinguish successful edits from subtle preservation failures while remaining efficient enough for repeated online evaluation.
blocks.zh: RL提供了一个培训后机制,以优化视觉发电机,防止超出监督重建目标的反馈。 DDPO和DPOK为传播模式确立政策分级方法[Black等,2024年;Fan等,2023年];Flow-GRPO和DanceGRPO将群相优化推广到以流为主和更广泛的视觉生成环境[Liu等,2025年a;Xue等,2025年];而DifmulationNFT通过前瞻过程制定在线奖励驱动更新[Zheng等,2026年]. 在这些基础的基础上,编辑专用方法越来越强调奖励反馈的设计. HIVE学习了人类的喜好来指导指导编辑[Zhang等,2024a]. UniWorld-V2结合了DifmusionNFT与以MLLM登录为基础的反馈和分组过滤,以稳定编辑优化[Li等,2025]. Edit-R1训练了基于原则的推理验证员,并利用其奖励与GRPO优化了编辑模型[郭等,2026]. 在系统一级,Swift-Image将平行的专家RL和多教师政策分解结合起来,以减轻不同目标之间的干扰[Hu等,2026a]。 这些办法共同激励人们作出奖励,可靠地将成功的编辑与微妙的保存失败区分开来,同时保持足够高效,可重复在线评价。

blocks.en: Regression-based reward models learn holistic or dimension-specific preferences from vision-language representations, commonly through regression or pairwise preference objectives. ImageReward, PickScore, and HPS/HPSv2 model human preferences for text-to-image generation [ Xu et al., 2023 , Kirstain et al., 2023 , Wu et al., 2023b , Wu et al., 2023a ] ; MPS extends evaluation to multiple dimensions [ Zhang et al., 2024b ] , while HPSv3 explores broader visual preference modeling [ Ma et al., 2025 ] . For image editing, HIVE and EditReward learn editing-specific preference signals [ Zhang et al., 2024a , Wu et al., 2026 ] , and ADIEE develops automated editing evaluation [ Chen et al., 2025 ] . Avoiding lengthy rationale generation makes direct scoring attractive for online RL. However, scores alone do not explicitly expose which concrete editing or preservation requirements are satisfied, motivating richer supervision during reward learning.
blocks.zh: 基于回归的奖励模式从视觉语言表述中学习整体或维度特定偏好,通常通过回归或对等偏好目标来学习. Image Reward, PickScore, 和HPS/HPSv2模式人类对文本到图像生成的偏好 [徐等, 2023年; Kirstain等, 2023年; Wu等, 2023b; Wu等, 2023a]; MPS将评价扩展到多维度 [张等, 2024b];而HPSv3探索更广泛的视觉偏好模式 [马等, 2025]. 对于图像编辑,HIVE和Edit Reward学习特定编辑偏好信号[. Zhang等, 2024a., Wu等, 2026], ADIEE开发出自动编辑评价[Chen等, 2025]. 避免冗长的原理生成使得直接得分对在线RL具有吸引力. 然而,单靠分数并不能明确揭露哪些具体的编辑或保存要求得到满足,从而促使在奖励学习期间进行更丰富的监督。

blocks.en: Generative reward models make evaluation more explicit by producing rationales or structured critiques. EditScore, RationalRewards, SpatialReward, and UnifiedReward-Think investigate reasoning-based visual assessment from complementary perspectives [ Luo et al., 2026 , Wang et al., 2026a , Long et al., 2026 , Wang et al., 2025a ] . Such reasoning can provide detailed diagnostic evidence, but autoregressive evaluation introduces additional computation when repeated across online RL samples. JRM and Z-Reward address this efficiency challenge by internalizing reasoning into more direct reward prediction pathways [ Yang et al., 2026 , Jin et al., 2026 ] . Our focus is on the supervision transferred into such efficient predictors: instance-specific verification requirements grounded in both the source image and the editing instruction.
blocks.zh: 基因奖励模式通过提出理由或结构性批评,使评价更加明确。 EditScore,Reasonnal Rewards, Space Rewards, and UnitedReward-Think 从互补角度调查基于推理的视觉评估[Luo等,2026年;Wang等,2026年a;Long等,2026年;Wang等,2025年a]. 这种推理可以提供详细的诊断证据,但自回评价在跨在线RL样本重复时引入了额外的计算. JRM和Z-Reward通过将推理内部化成为更直接的奖励预测路径来应对这一效率挑战[杨等,2026年;龚等,2026年]. 我们的重点是将监督转移到这种高效的预测器上:基于源图像和编辑指令的个案核查要求。

blocks.en: Adaptive evaluation tailors its criteria to individual inputs. RubricRM generates input-specific dimensions, weights, and scoring criteria [ Kan et al., 2026 ] , while Edit-R1 decomposes editing instructions into principles for explicit verification [ Guo et al., 2026 ] . Generated checklists have also been studied for language-model evaluation [ Cook et al., 2024 ] ; in multimodal preference optimization, rDPO uses instance-specific checklist-style rubrics to construct and filter preference data [ Yu et al., 2026 ] . CheckDistill combines adaptive verification with efficient reward inference: source-image-grounded atomic checklists and their verification evidence serve as privileged information during reward-model training. Distilling this supervision into direct multidimensional score distributions enables reward prediction without checklist inputs or explicit reasoning at deployment.
blocks.zh: 适应性评价使其标准适合个人投入。 RubricRM生成出特定输入维度,分量,和评分标准[Kan等,2026],而Edit-R1则将编辑指令分解为明确核查的原则[Guo等,2026]. 还研究了生成的核对表,用于语言模型评价[Cook等,2024];在多模式优惠优化中,rDPO使用实例特定核对表风格的路由来构建并过滤偏好数据[Yu等,2026]. CheckDistill将适应性核查与高效的奖励推论结合起来:来源-图像基础原子清单及其核查证据在奖励模式培训中作为特权信息. 将这种监督下放到直接的多维分数分配中,就可以在没有核对表投入或部署时明确推理的情况下作出奖励预测。

blocks.en: Given one or more reference images and an editing instruction, the checklist constructor generates atomic verification items for Instruction Following (IF), Attribute Preservation (AP), and Context Preservation (CP). Each item contains five key fields: type , indicating the evaluation dimension; object , specifying the edited or preserved entity; location , describing its spatial position; bbox_2d , giving the normalized bounding box in the reference image; and content , specifying the atomic requirement to be verified. Bounding-box coordinates are normalized to integer values in [ 0 , 1000 ] [0,1000] , and bbox_2d is set to null for newly added objects when no expected generation region can be determined. For multiple reference images, ref_image further identifies the source image containing the object. The checklist is returned as a single JSON list, as specified in the template below.
blocks.zh: 鉴于一个或多个参考图像和编辑指令,清单构建器生成原子核查项目,用于指令跟踪(IF)、属性保存(AP)和上下文保存(CP)。 每个项目包含五个关键字段: 类型,表示评价维度; 对象,指定被编辑或保存的实体; 位置,描述其空间位置; bbox_2d,在参考图像中给出已规范的边框; 内容,指定需要验证的原子要求. Bbounding-box坐标在 [0, 1000] [0, 1100] 中被正常化为整数,当无法确定预期生成区域时,bbox_2d被设定为新添加的对象无效. 对于多个参考图像,ref_image会进一步识别包含对象的源图像. 核对表作为单一的JSON列表返回,如下模板所说明.

blocks.en: ⬇ You are a strict and meticulous expert in designing image - editing checklists . Given one or more reference images and an editing instruction , generate checklists that can guide subsequent evaluation . **## Input ** Prompt : { request } Image input : one or more reference images < image > **## Generation Procedure ** 1. Inspect the reference image ( s ): describe key elements that are actually visible in the reference image ( s ), including their location , count , color , shape , pose , and other observable attributes . Do not infer or imagine any invisible content . 2. Parse the instruction : decompose the editing request into concrete add / remove / modify operations . 3. Generate checklists : decompose each operation into independently verifiable checklist items . **## Checklist Types ** - Instruction Following ( IF ): the specific editing action that must be performed on an object involved in the edit . - Attribute Preservation ( AP ): the key attributes of an edited object that should remain unchanged during editing . - Context Preservation ( CP ): for each object not involved in the edit , set the content to " Keep this object unchanged ." **## Generation Rules ( Must Be Followed )** 1. ** Groundedness **: The object , location , and content in every checklist item must be directly grounded in either the visible content of the reference image ( s ) or the explicit editing instruction . Do not introduce objects , attributes , or locations that are unsupported by either the reference image ( s ) or the editing instruction . 2. ** Atomicity **: Each checklist item must describe only one independently verifiable target . Do not combine multiple operations , objects , or attributes into a single item . 3. ** Removal Operations **: Specify only the object to be removed and its location . Do not describe how the background should be filled after removal . 4. ** BBox Localization **: Each checklist item must include ‘ bbox_2d ‘, indicating the bounding box of the object in the reference image in the format [ x1 , y1 , x2 , y2 ], where the coordinates correspond to the top - left and bottom - right corners and are normalized to integer values in [0, 1000]. The ‘ bbox_2d ‘ must tightly cover the actually visible extent of the object . When multiple reference images are provided , additionally use ‘ ref_image ‘ to indicate the 1- based index of the reference image containing the object . For an IF item involving a newly added object that does not exist in the reference image , set ‘ bbox_2d ‘ to the expected generation region ; if the expected region cannot be determined , set it to null . 5. ** Self - Check **: Before output , verify that every checklist item is directly supported by either the reference image ( s ) or the editing instruction , and that each ‘ bbox_2d ‘ is consistent with the actual object location . **## Output ** Write all checklist items into a single JSON list . The output language must be consistent with the editing instruction : [ { " checklist_id ": IntType , " type ": " IF | AP | CP ", " object ": " object name ", " location ": " position in reference image ", " bbox_2d ": [ x1 , y1 , x2 , y2 ], " content ": " editing instruction or preservation constraint " }, … ]
blocks.zh: ⬇ 你是一个严格而细致的专家 设计图像 - 编辑清单。 考虑到一个或多个参考图像和编辑指示,生成可指导随后评价的清单。 **## 输入 ** 提示 : { 请求} 图像输入:一个或多个参考图像 < 图像 > **## 生成程序** 1. 检查参考图像(s):描述参考图像(s)中实际可见的关键元素,包括其位置,计数,颜色,形状,姿势等可观测属性. 不要推断或想象任何隐形内容。 2. 解析指令:将编辑请求分解为具体添加/去除/修改操作. . 3. 生成核对表:将每个操作分解为可独立核查的核对表项目。 **## 明细列表类型 ** - 指令跟随(IF ):在编辑中涉及的对象上必须执行的具体编辑动作. - 属性保存(AP):编辑时应保持不变的被编辑对象的关键属性。 - 上下文保存(CP):对于没有参与编辑的每个对象,设置内容为"保持此对象不变". **## 世代规则(必须遵守)** 1. ** 理由**: 每个清单项目中的对象、位置和内容必须直接基于参考图像的可见内容或明确的编辑指示。 不引入无法通过参考图像( s) 或编辑指令 支持的对象、 属性或位置 。 2. ** 原子**:每个清单项目只须说明一个可独立核查的目标。 不将多个操作、对象或属性合并为一个单项。 3. ** 搬运作业 **:仅指定要删除的对象及其位置。 不描述删除后应如何填入背景 。 4. ** BBox 本地化 **:每个清单项目必须包括`bbox_2d',在格式[x1,y1,x2,y2]的参考图像中表示对象的边框,其中坐标与上-左-下-右角相对应,并在 [0,1000] 中与整数正常化. `box_2d'必须严格覆盖物体的实际可见范围。 在提供多个参考图像时,另外使用 “ ref_image ” 来表示包含对象的参考图像的基于 1 的索引 。 对于涉及参考图像中不存在的新添加对象的IF项目,将 “ bbox_2d ” 设定为预期生成区域; 如果无法确定预期区域, 则设定为无效 。 页:1 自己 - 检查 ** **: 在输出前,验证每个清单项目直接由参考图像(s)或编辑指令所支持,并且每个‘box_2d'与实际对象位置一致. **## ** 将所有清单项目写入一个单独的JSON清单。 输出语言必须与编辑指令一致 : [{ " 核对表-id " :IntType, " 类型 " : " IF QQ AP QQ CP " , " 对象 " : " 对象名称 " , " 位置 " : " 参考图像中的位置 " , " bbox_2d " : [x1, y1, x2, y2], " 内容 " : " 编辑指令或保存约束 " ], .]

blocks.en: We use two complementary judges for semantic consistency (SC) and perceptual quality (PQ). The SC judge performs instance-specific, checklist-guided evaluation using the editing instruction, generated checklist, reference image(s), and edited result. It independently assesses Instruction Following (IF), Attribute Preservation (AP), and Context Preservation (CP), and outputs checklist-level judgments, dimension-wise scores and rationales, and an overall SC score. The PQ judge instead evaluates the edited result alone under a fixed quality rubric covering sharpness, generation artifacts, structural plausibility, lighting and perspective consistency, and boundary blending, and outputs a perceptual-quality score with a concise rationale. The complete prompt templates are provided below.
blocks.zh: 我们在语义一致性(SC)和知觉质量(PQ)方面使用两个互补的判断. 最高法院法官利用编辑指导、生成清单、参考图像和编辑结果进行针对具体案例的、清单指导的评估。 它独立评估了以下指令(IF)、属性保全(AP)和上下文保全(CP),以及产出清单一级的判断、分量和理由,以及整个SC分数。 而PQ法官则在固定的质量标题下单独评价所编辑的结果,内容包括锐度、出厂文物、结构合理性、照明和视角一致性以及边界混合,并以简明的理由输出一个感知质量分数。 下文提供了完整的快速模板。

blocks.en: ⬇ You are a strict and consistent expert in image - editing quality evaluation . Your task is to assign absolute quality scores for instruction following and context preservation of an edited result . **## Input ** Prompt : { request } Checklists : { checklists_json } Image input order : one or more reference images ( from the first image to the second - to - last image ) -> edited result image ( the last image ) **## Evaluation Rules ( Must Be Followed )** 1. ** Checklist Evaluation **: Evaluate every provided checklist item one by one . Do not introduce additional evaluation criteria , and do not speculate about details that are not visible in the images . 2. ** Visible Evidence Only **: Every judgment must be based only on differences that can be directly observed between the reference image ( s ) and the edited result . You may use the checklist ‘ bbox_2d ‘ ([ x1 , y1 , x2 , y2 ], normalized to [0, 1000]) to localize the corresponding object in the reference image before comparing it with the relevant region in the edited result . 3. ** Independent Scoring **: Score Instruction Following ( IF ), Attribute Preservation ( AP ), and Context Preservation ( CP ) independently . Performance in one dimension must not compensate for errors in another . 4. ** Stronger Penalty for Incorrect Edits **: Editing the wrong object , introducing malformed structures , causing structural collapse , or violating physical plausibility should be penalized more heavily than simply failing to perform an intended edit . 5. ** Full Satisfaction Criterion **: A checklist item is considered fully satisfied only when both conditions hold : the requested edit or preservation constraint is correctly satisfied , and the corresponding region is visually free of defects . **## Scoring Scale ( Shared by IF , AP , and CP ; Integer Scores from 0 to 9)** First estimate the fraction of checklist items satisfied within the dimension , then determine the score by considering the severity of the observed defects : - 9: All requirements are fully satisfied , with no visible defects . - 8: All requirements are satisfied , with only minor imperfections in a small number of non - critical aspects . - 7: All critical requirements are completed , while a few non - critical aspects are not fully satisfied . - 6: Most requirements are satisfied , with noticeable but non - severe defects . - 5: Roughly two - thirds of the requirements are satisfied , or there is one clear defect . - 4: Roughly half of the requirements are satisfied , or there are multiple clear defects . - 3: Only a small portion is satisfied , or there is one severe defect , such as editing the wrong object , deformation , or structural collapse . - 2: Very few requirements are satisfied , or there are multiple severe defects . - 1: Almost none of the requirements are satisfied , with severe incorrect edits . - 0: The requested edit or preservation constraint is entirely unfulfilled or completely incorrect . ** Discriminability Requirement **: Use the full 0-9 score range . Do not cluster scores around 5-7 without sufficient evidence . Scores must clearly distinguish among perfect results (9), minor imperfections (7-8), noticeable defects (4-6), and severe failures (0-3). Final ‘ score ‘: compute an overall score with IF as the primary factor and AP / CP as secondary factors . The score may be a floating - point value with one decimal place . If IF <= 3, the final score must not exceed 4. **## Output ( Strict JSON Only ; Use the Same Language as the Editing Instruction )** - ‘ ckl reason ‘: provide a judgment rationale for every checklist item without omission . - ‘ IF reason ‘, ‘ AP reason ‘, ‘ CP reason ‘, and the overall ‘ reason ‘: summarize all relevant observations within the corresponding dimension , using the object as the grammatical subject whenever possible . - Order observations by their impact on the score , from largest to smallest . Keep the explanations concise and non - redundant . { " ckl reason ": " string ", " IF score ": <0-9 int >, " IF reason ": " string ", " AP score ": <0-9 int >, " AP reason ": " string ", " CP score ": <0-9 int >, " CP reason ": " string ", " score ": <0-9 float >, " reason ": " string " } ⬇ You are a strict and consistent expert in image quality evaluation . Your task is to assign an absolute score based solely on the visual quality of the edited result itself , independent of whether the editing instruction has been successfully fulfilled . **## Input ** Prompt : { request } Image input : edited result image **## Evaluation Rules ( Must Be Followed )** 1. Base all judgments only on directly observable evidence in the image . Do not speculate about nonexistent content , and do not over - penalize negligible imperfections . 2. Inspect the image in the following order : (* @ \ ding {172} @ *) sharpness / noise / blur (* @ \ ding {173} @ *) artifacts / compositing misalignment / unnatural textures (* @ \ ding {174} @ *) deformation or structural errors in humans and objects (* @ \ ding {175} @ *) consistency of lighting / perspective / color (* @ \ ding {176} @ *) edge blending and overall realism 3. First identify the defects that are actually present , then assign a score according to the scale below . **## Scoring Scale ( Integer Scores from 0 to 9)** - 9: Highly realistic and natural , with sharp image quality , no visible defects , and rich details . - 8: Excellent quality , with only one minor imperfection that does not affect the overall viewing experience . - 7: Good quality , with a small number of minor imperfections that do not materially affect the overall appearance . - 6: Acceptable quality , with noticeable imperfections that slightly affect the viewing experience . - 5: Average quality , with multiple imperfections or one clear defect . - 4: Poor quality , with multiple clear defects , such as local artifacts or mild deformation . - 3: Bad quality , with severe defects such as obvious deformation , structural errors , or large - scale artifacts . - 2: Very poor quality , with multiple severe defects that substantially degrade the visual result . - 1: Severely distorted , with major structural collapse and little practical usability . - 0: Completely unusable , corrupted , or visually unrecognizable . ** Discriminability Requirement **: Use the full 0-9 score range . Do not cluster scores around 5-7 without sufficient evidence . Assign high scores (8-9) when no meaningful defects are present , and confidently assign low scores (0-3) when severe defects are observed . **## Output ( Strict JSON Only ; Use the Same Language as the Editing Instruction )** The ‘ reason ‘ field should briefly summarize the main defects or strengths that determine the score : { " score ": <0-9 int >, " reason ": " string " } """

QQ Out(严格 JSON Only; 使用与"编辑指令"相同的语言)** - `ckl 理由':为每个清单项目提供判断理由,而不遗漏. - `IF 理由',`AP 理由',`CP 理由',以及总体"理由":在相应维度内总结所有相关观察,尽可能将对象作为语法主题. - 按其对分数的影响排列观测,从最大到最小. 保持解释简洁和不冗余。 { " ckl reason " : " string " , " IF分数 " : <0-9英寸; "IF分数 " : <0-9英寸; " AP分数 " : <0-9英寸; " AP分数 " : <0-9英寸; "CP分数 " : <0-9浮动; " 理由 " : < 字符串 " }} 你是一个严格和一致的图像质量评估专家。 您的任务就是根据编辑结果本身的视觉质量来分配绝对分数, **## 输入 ** 提示 : { 请求} 图像输入: 编辑结果图像 评价规则(必须遵守)** 1. 所有判决仅以图像中的直接可观察证据为依据。 请不要猜测不存在的内容, 2.按下顺序检查图像:(*@\ d {172};*)锐利/噪声/模糊(*#173};*)文物/堆肥错位/不自然纹理(*##174};*)人和物体的变形或结构出错(*##175};*)灯光一致性/视角/颜色(*#叮{176};*)边缘混合和整体现实主义. 3. 首先查明实际存在的缺陷,然后根据以下比额表分配分数。 **## 分数表(整数分数从0到9)** - 9:高度现实和自然,具有尖锐的图像质量,没有明显的缺陷,而且细节丰富。 - 说吧 8:优秀品质,只有一点小不完美,不影响整体取景经验. - 7:质量良好,少数小的不完善,对整体外观没有实质影响。 - 6:可接受质量,明显不完善,略微影响取景经验。 - 5: 平均质量,有多重缺陷或一个明显的缺陷。 - 4: 质量差,有多重明显的缺陷,例如当地文物或轻微变形。 - 3:质量差,有明显变形等严重缺陷,结构出错,或有大尺度文物. 2. 质量极差,存在多种严重缺陷,严重地使视觉结果退化。 - 说吧 1. 严重扭曲,结构严重崩溃,实际可用性不大。 - 0:完全无法使用、腐败或视而不见。 页:1 歧视性要求 **:使用0-9分全分范围. 没有足够证据, 当不存在有意义的缺陷时,分配高分(8-9分),当观察到严重缺陷时,自信地分配低分(0-3)。 QQ 输出( 仅严格 JSON; 使用与编辑指令相同的语言) ** `理由'字段应简要总结决定分数的主要缺陷或长处:{ "分数":<0-9英寸>,"理由":"弦"}".

blocks.en: The same scoring prompt is used for Stage-I supervised fine-tuning and for the student model in Stage-II CR-OPSD. Given the editing instruction, one or more reference images, and the edited result, the model independently predicts four absolute scores for Instruction Following (IF), Attribute Preservation (AP), Context Preservation (CP), and Perceptual Quality (PQ). The model outputs the four integer scores in a fixed order, as specified below.
blocks.zh: 同样的分数提示用于第一阶段监督的微调和第二阶段CR-OPSD的学生模型. 考虑到编辑指令,一个或多个参考图像,以及被编辑的结果,模型独立预测了四个绝对分数,分别是"指令跟随"(IF),"属性保存"(AP),"上下文保存"(CP)和"概念质量"(PQ). 该模型以固定顺序输出四个整数分数,具体如下.

blocks.en: ⬇ You are a strict and consistent image editing quality judge . Based on the editing instruction ( Prompt ), compare the reference image ( s ) with the result image , and assign absolute quality scores along four independent dimensions : Instruction Following ( IF ), Attribute Preservation ( AP ), Context Preservation ( CP ), and Perceptual Quality ( PQ ). **## Input ** Prompt : { request } Image input order : one or more reference images ( from the first to the second - to - last ) (* @$ \ rightarrow$@ *) the result image ( the last one ) { image_tags } **## Judging Rules ( must be followed )** 1. ** Visible facts only **: All scoring must be based on visual differences directly observable between the reference image ( s ) and the result image . Never speculate about details that do not exist in the images , and do not exaggerate minor flaws . 2. ** Independent scoring **: IF , AP , CP , and PQ must each be scored independently , with no compensation between them . 3. ** PQ is Prompt - independent **: PQ evaluates only the result image ’ s own visual quality , independent of how well the editing instruction ( Prompt ) is fulfilled . 4. ** Maintain score discrimination **: Make full use of the 0-9 score range and avoid clustering scores at 5-7 without justification . 9 indicates perfect performance , 7-8 indicates minor issues , 4-6 indicates obvious defects , and 0-3 indicates severe failure . **## Evaluation Dimensions ** - ** Instruction Following ( IF )**: Evaluates whether the editing result fulfills the Prompt requirements . Focus on whether the edited object is correct , whether the edited content meets the requirements , whether the target attribute modifications are accurate , whether the degree of editing is sufficient , and whether there are missed edits , wrong edits , or clearly unreasonable results . - ** Attribute Preservation ( AP )**: Evaluates whether the attributes of the edited object that the Prompt does not require to change remain consistent . Focus on whether non - target attributes such as object identity , appearance , color , structure , position , pose , quantity , proportion , material , and texture are preserved . - ** Context Preservation ( CP )**: Evaluates whether objects not involved in the Prompt , the background , and the overall image properties such as color tone , lighting , and composition remain consistent with the reference image ( s ). - ** Perceptual Quality ( PQ )**: Evaluates the result image ’ s own visual quality and overall impression . Focus on whether the fundamental image quality ( sharpness , blurriness , noise ) is good ; whether there are generation artifacts ( unnatural textures , stitching misalignment , etc .), deformations , or physics - violating phenomena ; whether human or object structures are plausible ; whether lighting , shadows , perspective , reflections , and colors are harmonious and consistent ; whether the background blends naturally with the subject ; whether textures and edges look natural ; and the overall realism , aesthetics , and detail quality . **## Scoring Scale ( integer , 0-9)** **### Instruction Following ( IF )** 9: Fully follows the Prompt . The edited object is correct , all requirements are accurately completed , and the result looks natural . 0: The edit is not performed at all , or is performed completely incorrectly : the edited object is wrong , the edited content is contrary or irrelevant to the Prompt requirements , or the editing result is severely deformed or structurally broken . **### Attribute Preservation ( AP )** 9: The edited object remains highly consistent ; only the attributes explicitly required by the Prompt are changed , and all non - target attributes are preserved . 0: The non - target attributes of the edited object are severely lost ; its identity or structure is completely changed and it can no longer be recognized as the same object in the reference image ( s ). **### Context Preservation ( CP )** 9: The non - edited content remains completely consistent , with no observable changes . 0: The non - edited content is largely destroyed or entirely repainted , with almost no consistency with the reference image ( s ). **### Perceptual Quality ( PQ )** 9: Realistic and natural ; sharp fundamental quality with no blurring , noise , artifacts , deformations , or physics violations ; plausible structure ; harmonious lighting and color ; rich detail . 0: Severely distorted ; pervasive deformations , generation artifacts , quality defects , and physics errors ; broken structure ; essentially unusable . **## Output :** [ IF score , AP score , CP score , PQ score ]

blocks.en: Appendix J Discussion
blocks.zh: 附录J 讨论情况

blocks.en:
Z-Reward [ Jin et al., 2026 ] and our CheckDistill both distill reasoning-supported assessment into direct scoring, but address different challenges.
Z-Reward focuses on representing preference uncertainty and fine-grained score differences through reasoning-conditioned score distributions. Our starting point is that image-editing evaluation requires instance-specific verification of both requested changes and preservation constraints. We therefore introduce Dynamic Checklist Scaling to translate each editing instruction and source image into atomic verification criteria, enriching the teacher context with checklists and their supporting judgements.
blocks.zh:
Z-Reward [Jin等,2026] 和我们的"CheckDistill"都把推理支持的评估提炼成直接评分,但解决了不同的挑战.
Z-Reward专注于通过推理条件分数分配来代表偏好不确定性和精细分数差异. 我们的出发点是,图像编辑评价要求对所要求的修改和保存方面的限制进行具体核查。 因此,我们采用动态核对清单缩放法,将每个编辑指示和源图像转化为原子核查标准,用核对表及其辅助判断丰富教师背景。

blocks.en:
This focus on verification evidence also shapes our distillation design.
While Z-Reward transfers scoring knowledge from a large reasoning teacher to a compact student, we use on-policy self-distillation with an evidence-enriched teacher of the same architecture.
Distribution-Aligned Context Compression transfers the teacher’s scoring behavior at student-generated prefixes, and reliability weighting modulates supervision at score positions according to teacher–label agreement, accounting for potentially incorrect teacher judgements. Our contribution centers on constructing and reliably internalizing instance-specific verification evidence , enabling direct scoring without checklist inputs or explicit reasoning at inference time.
blocks.zh:
这种注重核查证据的做法也塑造了我们的蒸馏设计。
Z-Reward将知识从一个大型推理老师转移到一个紧凑的学生身上, 我们用一个在政策上自我消化的老师,
